summary: Clearwater NF lookout two miles south of Lochsa Ranger Station: 1930 tree-top observatory, 1931 L-4 cab; last staffed 1941; burned early 1950s; no source describes remains.

facts.design: L-4 cab on an 8-foot log crib (1931), first an observatory in a fir tree top (1930)
facts.status_note: Usable lumber salvaged and the rest burned, in the early 1950s or 1953; no source describes what remains

events.note: Observatory built in the cut-off top of a fir tree about 65 feet up; crow's nest established in 1930
L-4 cab erected atop an 8-foot log crib
Earnest Hartman and Harry Chenoweth are the names listed for 1930
Abandoned after the 1941 season; firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts say 1940s
Usable lumber salvaged, then the rest burned; the Forest Lookouts copy of Hartig's text says early 1950s

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Service list, firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts date the L-4 cab to 1931; the Nez Perce-Clearwater Facebook post says the lookout was built in 1930. The story gives 1930 for the tree-top observatory and 1931 for the cab, and says one account dates the whole lookout to 1930.
Forest Lookouts quotes Hartig as early 1950s; the Facebook post quotes Hartig as 1953. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Gone; location, cab design and 1931 cab date agree across four sources. Date conflicts are reported in the story: the cab is 1931 in three sources but the Facebook copy says the lookout was built in 1930; burning is early 1950s in the Forest Lookouts copy of Hartig and 1953 in the Facebook copy. The brief's height_m 19.8 equals 65 feet, the tree-top crow's nest, so it is proposed for removal. No source describes what remains at the site or whether it is open to the public, so access is omitted. The Facebook post repeats Hartig's 1981 history and is the only source for 1953 and the 1930 build date. The 1940s abandonment date is consistent with the 1941 last season. About 7 page reads and 1 WebSearch, slightly over the per-tower read budget, because the PDF and Facebook copies were needed to settle the dates.
